item.title: Sunday, September 6, 2026 - How did a glacier collapse lead to the deadly disaster in Nepal? Was there something about the area that caused the collapse? How much can we say this disaster is a climate disaster? Did climate change cause this glacier collapse?
item.description: We seek to elevate the discourse of contemporary issues and discuss the globe's challenges with scholars and researchers from all over the world.
item.itunes:summary: Guest: Umesh Haritashya is Director of the Sustainability Program and Professor of Earth, Environment and Sustainability at the University of Dayton, Ohio, Mathias Vuille is Distinguished Professor in the Department of Atmospheric and Environmental Sciences, University at Albany, SUNY and Bethan Davies is Professor of Glaciology in the Department of Geography at Newcastle University. You can hear this and other interviews at www.scholarscircle.org

item.title: Sunday, August 23, 2026 - Wildfires have been raging in North America, Europe and South America and have grown significantly worse worldwide. Is the worsening of these fires due to climate change? And what needs to be done to either mitigate or adapt to these new realities?

item.title: Sunday, August 16, 2026 - Does the world's aging population mean fewer wars in the future? What exactly is a geriatric peace? Then, we explore a new book on the peaceful uses of nuclear power.

item.title: Sunday, August 9, 2026 - The Greater Horn of Africa, in Northeastern Africa, faces a severe food insecurity. In Sudan 19 million-plus people facing acute hunger 825,000 children under 5 expected to suffer from Severe Acute Malnutrition in 2026. And 12-14 million people severely food insecure in Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia. What are the root causes and immediate effects of this famine? How can the world help address food insecurity in this region? Then, The United Kingdom has a new Prime Minister. He is the 7th Prime Minister in the last decade, a remarkable instability for the nation. First of all, who is Andy Burnham? Why did he replace Kier Starmer? Why has the UK had such instability? Is it because of the decision to leave the EU, or what is called Brexit? And what does Burnhams leadership suggest for the future of the UK?
item.description: We seek to elevate the discourse of contemporary issues and discuss the globe's challenges with scholars and researchers from all over the world.
